Proof of the loop case sing_eq_of_le_of_le_of_stronglyCausalOn_e0 (§2b of AbsMax): (1) prop:isom near the axis, e0Loop_localForm: every e in e0Groupoid is, on a ball around an axis point, (tau,z) -> (tau+a, R z), R a linear isometry of C — Rigid's local core re-proved as e0Loop_core_of_region to export F, F P = P^k F, k^2 = 1; lam = 1 (e0Loop_lam_eq_one: the angle of D^-1 F D is lam(nu + kappa theta), kappa^2 = 1 by nullQ, one turn gives lam kappa = k); paper coordinates (e0Loop_paper_form); rigidity e0_rigid. (2) ShadowRel a b between BTZ points (horizontal discs of the preferred charts, point by point up to an isometry), reflexive, transitive, local along a rising axis piece (chart_le_iff + calculus_le, vertical null lines chart_le_vertical, transitions exists_transition_axis), global along every BTZ causal curve by a sup argument (shadowRel_of_curve) — this replaces the paper's finite chart covering. (3) Pigeonhole on the compact circle (exists_iterate_near) replaces Dirichlet / the rational case. (4) Contradiction: p regular near x <= q near y <= points of p's shadow back near x arbitrarily close to p (no Minkowski-interval estimate needed: the return is exact up to the isometry), against causal convexity in A of a neighbourhood of p (le_of_le_of_notMem_sing moves the relations into A). Remark (not a paper finding): GX's Rigid leaves the winding k = -1 (a reflection (tau,z) -> (tau+a, e^{ib} conj z)) open; the proof does not need to exclude it, since the return map is handled as an arbitrary linear isometry R of C (a reflection return closes after two turns).

B21 l.975–979 asserts j∘i⁻¹(W) ⊆ U from I⁺(q′) ∩ I⁻(j(bₙ)) ⊂ U, but the argument only gives j(W) ⊆ J⁺(q′) ∩ J⁻(j(bₙ)) (a limit of chronological relations is causal), so the step needs the CAUSAL diamonds J(q′, j(bₙ)) to shrink into U: true in a GH M₂ (compact, nested, intersection {q′} by causality and closedness of J^±); formalized that way (WP-43c). B21 l.980 'W is the regular part of a neighborhood of some point of sing(E₀)': W = I⁺(p) ∩ I⁻(bₙ) contains no neighbourhood of p itself; it contains the regular part of a neighbourhood of a BTZ point z strictly above p on the line, close enough to p to lie in I⁻(bₙ) (exists_sing_above, exists_nhds_diff_sing_subset_Iplus via SingularPastAt and Iplus_of_lt). findings: Direction (ii)⇒(i) is sorry-free and (i)⇒(ii) reduces exactly to lemma K's local input: the paper's covering-space argument (φ a covering, ψ a section, π₁ onto, O'Neill Lemma 45, intersection numbers) is not needed once the image of the compact Cauchy surface is locally Cauchy.

The connectedness of a compact acausal Cauchy surface of a connected GH spacetime (needed by lemma K; implicit in B21, whose Σ is a genus-g surface) holds without any splitting: isConnected_of_isCauchySurface_abstract (model-free: tarentin, causally arc-connected, CurvesExtend, T2).

B21 l.1044–1046's definition of E_A-maximality, read literally (no connectedness of N), is satisfied by NO nonempty M: for any nonempty globally hyperbolic E_A-manifold M', the inclusion M ↪ M ⊔ M' is an embedding (an a.e. E-morphism) into a globally hyperbolic E_A-manifold (causal relations do not cross components, so it stays causal with compact diamonds) and is not onto. Hence the 'without loss of generality … M and N are connected' of l.1058 is not without loss of generality: connectedness of N must be part of the definition. IsE0Maximal builds it in. Counterexample given in prose, not formalized (would need the 𝔼₀-atlas of a disjoint union).
